findings.summary: crates/server/src/github_app.rs:96: when GitHub hands out a token with under MARGIN (300 s) left, every request mints a new one, because nothing caches it past the margin. In e2e with 50 s tokens this was 6 mints a read. Real tokens last an hour so this is harmless in practice, but nothing stops it.

crates/server/src/github_app.rs:91: the tokens mutex is held across the installation lookup and mint HTTP calls. Reads are sequential today so nothing is blocked, but concurrent reads later would serialize on one repo's mint.
